title: two at once
subtitle: you can feel more than one thing

steps.text: feelings don't take turns. they show up together, and one small word lets them all be true.

steps.prompt: starting something new. try each one on:
steps.question: which one feels the most complete?
steps.reply: "and" doesn't make you pick. it lets the whole picture in.

steps.text: a friend moves away. you say, "i'm so happy for her, and i'm going to miss her a lot." both are real. neither cancels the other.

steps.prompt: make a two-at-once sentence. any pair works, even ones that seem opposite.

phrases: part of me ___, and part of me ___.
i love this, and it's a lot.
i'm okay, and it's been hard.

steps.prompt: one small thing for today, if you want:
options: next time a feeling shows up, check if another one came with it.
say one "and" sentence out loud, to someone or just to yourself.

steps.text: that's "and." more than one thing can be true, and you get to say all of it.

grounding.idea: describing feelings precisely is linked to healthier coping and can be practiced
grounding.source: Kashdan, Barrett & McKnight, 2015, Current Directions in Psychological Science
